## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the proper use, volume setting, tip loading,
sample aspiration and dispensing, and care of Gilson Pipetman
micropipettes. Micropipettes are precision instruments used to transfer
small volumes of liquid (less than 1 mL) with high accuracy. Correct
technique is essential for reproducible results in chemical, biological,
and environmental analyses.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All Gilson Pipetman micropipettes (P10, P20, P200,
  P1000) in the EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Serological pipettes, Pasteur pipettes, bottle-
  top dispensers, or Repipet-type dispensers
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure annual calibration      |
| Lab Manager       | Schedule calibration, maintain tip inventory |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Liquids being pipetted may be hazardous. Consult the
  relevant SOP and Safety Data Sheet for the material being transferred.
- **Physical:** Repetitive pipetting can cause repetitive strain
  injuries. Take breaks during extended pipetting sessions.
- **Biological:** When pipetting biological samples, use filter tips to
  prevent aerosol contamination of the pipette barrel.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

If hazardous liquid enters the pipette barrel, stop immediately.
Decontaminate the pipette per the manufacturer's instructions and refer
to [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item              | Volume Range        | Notes                        |
|:------------------|:--------------------|:-----------------------------|
| Pipetman P10      | 1.0 -- 10.0 $\mu$L     | Yellow or white tip          |
| Pipetman P20      | 2.0 -- 20.0 $\mu$L     | Yellow tip                   |
| Pipetman P200     | 20 -- 200 $\mu$L       | Yellow tip                   |
| Pipetman P1000    | 200 -- 1000 $\mu$L     | Blue tip                     |

### Consumables

| Item                          | Notes                                     |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Disposable pipette tips       | Match tip size to pipette; see Section 6.3 |
| Filter pipette tips           | Required for biological or volatile samples |
| Tip waste container           | Benchtop receptacle for used tips          |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Selecting the Correct Pipette

Always select the smallest pipette that covers the target volume. using
an unnecessarily large pipette for a small volume reduces accuracy. The
volume ranges are:

| Pipette  | Range             | Smallest Graduation |
|:---------|:------------------|:--------------------|
| P10      | 1.0 -- 10.0 $\mu$L   | 0.02 $\mu$L             |
| P20      | 2.0 -- 20.0 $\mu$L   | 0.02 $\mu$L             |
| P200     | 20 -- 200 $\mu$L     | 0.2 $\mu$L              |
| P1000    | 200 -- 1000 $\mu$L   | 2 $\mu$L                |

::: {.callout-important}
Never set the pipette below the minimum or above the maximum of its
range. Exceeding these limits will damage the piston seal and put the
pipette out of calibration.
:::

### 6.2 Setting the Volume

1. Identify the volume display window on the front face of the pipette.
   The three-digit display reads differently for each pipette size:
   - **P10:** digits represent ones, tenths, and hundredths of uL
   - **P20:** digits represent tens, ones, and tenths of uL
   - **P200:** digits represent hundreds, tens, and ones of uL
   - **P1000:** digits represent thousands, hundreds, and tens of uL
2. Turn the volume adjustment ring clockwise to increase volume or
   counterclockwise to decrease volume
3. If you overshoot the target while dialing down, dial below the
   desired setting and then dial back up to the correct value. This
   avoids mechanical backlash in the piston mechanism.

### 6.3 Loading a Tip

1. Select the correct tip size for the pipette being used. Tip boxes
   are labeled with the compatible pipette sizes. When in doubt, confirm
   with the lab manager.
2. Press the pipette shaft firmly into a tip in the tip box. A slight
   twist while pressing helps ensure a secure, airtight seal.
3. Do not touch the tip with your hands.
4. Always use a fresh tip for each different reagent or sample to
   prevent cross-contamination.

### 6.4 Aspirating (Loading) a Sample

1. Depress the plunger slowly to the **first stop** (the point of
   initial resistance). This is the calibrated load volume.
2. While holding the plunger at the first stop, immerse the tip into
   the liquid just enough to cover the opening (3--4 mm). Do not plunge
   the tip to the bottom of the vessel.
3. Slowly and steadily release the plunger to draw liquid into the tip.
   Do not let the plunger snap back.
4. Wait one to two seconds before removing the tip from the liquid,
   especially with viscous solutions. This allows the full volume to
   enter the tip and prevents air bubbles.
5. Visually inspect the tip: there should be no air gap or bubble at
   the distal end. If there is, dispense the liquid back and repeat.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
For viscous liquids (glycerol, concentrated DNA solutions), use the
"reverse pipetting" technique: depress the plunger to the **second
stop** before immersing the tip, draw up the liquid by releasing to the
rest position, and then dispense by pressing only to the **first stop**.
The small amount of liquid remaining in the tip is discarded.
:::

### 6.5 Dispensing a Sample

1. Touch the tip to the inner wall of the receiving vessel at a slight
   angle
2. Depress the plunger slowly to the **first stop** to dispense most of
   the liquid
3. Continue pressing to the **second stop** to expel the final drop
4. Hold the plunger at the second stop while withdrawing the tip from
   the vessel
5. Release the plunger only after the tip is clear of the liquid

### 6.6 Ejecting the Tip

1. Hold the pipette over the tip waste container
2. Press the tip ejector button on the back of the pipette
3. Never reuse a tip between different solutions

### 6.7 Important Precautions

- Never point a pipette upward with liquid in the tip. Liquid can flow
  back into the barrel and damage the piston and seals.
- Never lay a pipette down with a loaded tip.
- When not in use, set the pipette to its maximum volume and hang it
  vertically on the pipette stand. This relaxes the piston spring and
  extends the instrument's life.
- Do not use a pipette as a stirring rod.
- If the plunger action feels rough, sticky, or inconsistent, stop
  using the pipette and report the issue to the lab manager.


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 Gravimetric Accuracy Check

Verify pipette accuracy by weighing dispensed volumes of distilled water
on the analytical balance (see
[SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd)):

1. Tare a clean microcentrifuge tube on the analytical balance
2. Pipette the test volume of distilled water into the tube
3. Record the mass. At 20 C, 1 $\mu$L of water weighs approximately 1.00 mg.
4. Repeat for a total of 10 replicates
5. Calculate the mean and coefficient of variation (CV)

| Pipette | Test Volume | Acceptable CV   |
|:--------|:------------|:----------------|
| P10     | 10 $\mu$L       | less than 3%    |
| P20     | 20 $\mu$L       | less than 2%    |
| P200    | 200 $\mu$L      | less than 1%    |
| P1000   | 1000 $\mu$L     | less than 0.5%  |

If the CV exceeds the acceptable threshold, the pipette should be
removed from service and sent for professional calibration.

### 7.2 Calibration Schedule

All micropipettes must be professionally calibrated at least once per
year. Calibration stickers on each pipette show the date of last
calibration and the next due date. Do not use a pipette with an expired
calibration.


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| used pipette tips (non-hazardous) | Standard tip waste box; dispose in regular trash when full |
| used tips contaminated with hazardous chemicals | Chemical waste per [SOP-L003](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd) |
| used tips contaminated with biological material | Biohazard bag; autoclave before disposal |

## 10. Training Record

Before using micropipettes independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate correct volume setting, tip loading, aspiration, and
   dispensing technique under supervision
4. Perform a gravimetric accuracy check (Section 7.1) with acceptable
   results for at least two pipette sizes
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Volume Display Reading Guide {.appendix}

The three-digit volume display reads differently for each Pipetman size.
The table below shows the maximum display setting and the place value of
each digit:

| Pipette | Max Display | Digit 1 (top) | Digit 2 (middle) | Digit 3 (bottom) |
|:--------|:------------|:--------------|:------------------|:------------------|
| P10     | 1 0 . 0 0   | 10 $\mu$L         | 1 $\mu$L              | 0.1 $\mu$L            |
| P20     | 2 0 . 0     | 10 $\mu$L         | 1 $\mu$L              | 0.1 $\mu$L            |
| P200    | 2 0 0       | 100 $\mu$L        | 10 $\mu$L             | 1 $\mu$L              |
| P1000   | 1 0 0 0     | 1000 $\mu$L       | 100 $\mu$L            | 10 $\mu$L             |

## Appendix B: Troubleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Liquid drips from tip after aspiration | Tip not seated properly; damaged tip | Reseat or replace tip  |
| Air bubble in tip after aspiration | Plunger released too quickly; tip not immersed deep enough | Re-aspirate slowly with tip 3--4 mm below surface |
| Dispensed volume too low      | Pipette out of calibration; wrong tip size | Perform gravimetric check; verify tip compatibility |
| Plunger feels sticky or rough | Liquid entered barrel; worn piston seal | Clean barrel; send for service |
| Volume display will not turn  | Mechanical jam                  | Do not force; contact lab manager |
